original_title: Hydrogels in Pharmaceutical Formulation: Properties, formulation strategies, and drug delivery applications.
title: A hydrogels-in-pharma review, start to finish
blurb: A review rounding up hydrogel properties, how people formulate them, and where they end up in drug delivery. Reference material rather than a new finding.

original_title: Visible‐Light‐Induced Decarboxylative Cross‐Coupling Reactions: Transition‐Metal and Metal‐Free Approaches
title: Decarboxylative cross-coupling, now with and without metal
blurb: A review mapping visible-light decarboxylative cross-couplings, split between transition-metal photocatalysts running electron- and energy-transfer steps and the metal-free routes that skip the metal entirely. Useful survey of the field, not a new reaction of its own.

original_title: GSK partner Hansoh reports another phase 3 win for priority ADC - Fierce Biotech
title: Hansoh's ADC racks up another phase 3 win
blurb: GSK's partner Hansoh posts another positive phase 3 readout for their priority ADC. Headline only so far, no numbers to chew on yet.

original_title: Three Thiol-Reactive Reagents drive Synergistic Lethality in Glioblastoma cells.
title: Three thiol-reactive reagents team up against glioblastoma
blurb: A preprint reporting that combining three thiol-reactive reagents kills glioblastoma cells synergistically. It's a Research Square posting, so a lead, not a confirmed result.

original_title: Nitrosamine Impurities in Pharmaceuticals: Analytical Detection, Risk Assessment, and Quality Control Strategies
title: The nitrosamine mess, from valsartan to now
blurb: A review of detection, risk assessment, and QC for nitrosamine impurities, the genotoxic contaminants regulators have been chasing since the 2018 valsartan scare traced to a Chinese supplier. Acceptable intake sits at a punishing 26.6-96 ng/day under ICH M7, which is why every method in here has to be that sensitive.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Olaparib: Analytical methods for the quantification in drug substance, pharmaceutical formulations and biological matrices
title: Rounding up every way to measure olaparib
blurb: A review of analytical methods for quantifying the PARP inhibitor olaparib in drug substance, formulations, and biological matrices like plasma, urine, and tissue. The bookmark-for-later kind of paper, useful for QC and PK work rather than a read cover to cover.
venue: Journal of Liquid Chromatography & Related Technologies

original_title: Aziridination of inert alkanes via photo-mediated double hydrogen atom transfer
title: Turning unactivated C–H bonds straight into aziridines
blurb: A double hydrogen-atom-transfer route aziridinates inert alkanes directly, using photo-generated triplet sulfonyl nitrenes plus iodosobenzene. Bis-functionalizing unactivated alkanes normally takes several steps, this does it in one.

original_title: ADCs: How to manage complexities in growing supply chains - Pharmaceutical Technology
title: ADC supply chains are getting complicated
blurb: A trade piece on managing the growing complexity of ADC supply chains as more of these things reach commercial scale.

original_title: A Physical Organic Odyssey: From the Ultrafast Dynamics of Carbenes and Nitrenes to Contemporary Chemical Biology and Drug Discovery
title: Fifty years of carbenes, nitrenes, and photoaffinity probes, one birthday review
blurb: A tribute review for Matthew Platz's 75th, tracing how his ultrafast spectroscopy work on carbenes, nitrenes, and oxenium ions turned into the design rules behind today's photoaffinity labeling probes. More retrospective than new result, but a good one if you use PAL and never learned where the mechanistic groundwork came from.

original_title: White‐Light‐Mediated Imidazole Catalysis Toward Terpene‐Based Thermosets
title: Curing bio-based epoxies with a desk lamp and no photoinitiator
blurb: Limonene- and carvone-derived diepoxides cure under white light with glutaric anhydride and an imidazole catalyst, no photoinitiator needed, giving fully bio-based thermosets. NMR shows light also switches which epoxide ring opens, endo instead of the exo path you get from heat curing, so it's not just a gentler cure, it's a different mechanism.

original_title: Decarboxylative Chlorination of Cinnamic and Acetylenic Acids Enabled by a Vanadium-Dependent Chloroperoxidase
title: An enzyme swaps in for stoichiometric chlorination
blurb: A vanadium-dependent chloroperoxidase turns cinnamic and acetylenic acids into vinyl chlorides and chloroalkynes by decarboxylative chlorination, doing under mild conditions what usually takes harsh stoichiometric reagents. Yields are only moderate so far, but it's a catalytic route where basically none existed.

original_title: Photocatalytic Synthesis of Penem-type Pseudo-Natural Products Delivers a Novel Apo-IDO1 Inhibitor Chemotype
title: Photocatalysis builds a penem core and finds an IDO1 inhibitor along the way
blurb: Visible-light triplet energy transfer drives the first intermolecular [2+2] between alkenes and benzothiazoles, closing an azetidine ring onto a penem core and spinning out a library of pseudo-natural products across three scaffolds. One of them turned up as a new apo-IDO1 inhibitor chemotype, which is the kind of payoff this whole pseudo-natural-product strategy is supposed to deliver.

original_title: Synthesis of Tris(indol‐3‐yl)methanes From Indoles, CO 2 , and Dimethylphenylsilane With BPh 3 : Two‐Step Construction of π‐Conjugated Systems
title: Turning CO2 into the methine carbon of a tris(indolyl)methane
blurb: Indoles, CO2, and PhMe2SiH combine over BPh3 to build tris(indol-3-yl)methanes, and isotope labeling confirms the methine carbon and hydrogen come from the CO2 and silane respectively, the first CO2 fixation reaction to build that kind of aliphatic C-H group. DFT backs the proposed cascade mechanism, and the brominated product survives a follow-up palladium coupling, so it's not just a curiosity.

original_title: Inside Back Cover: A Cholesterol Analogue for Cell‐Surface Enzyme Display
title: A cholesterol analogue that displays enzymes on the cell surface
blurb: Cover art built around a cholesterol mimic designed to anchor and display enzymes at the cell surface.

original_title: VERAXA Biotech (NASDAQ: VRXA) Advances Bispecific ADC Program Under OmniAb Collaboration - The Globe and Mail
title: VERAXA keeps building out its bispecific ADC pipeline with OmniAb
blurb: VERAXA Biotech says it's advancing a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate program through its OmniAb collaboration. Standard press-release fare from a small-cap biotech, so read it as a pipeline update, not data.

original_title: ESCAPE: assigning site-specific activity to covalent ligands in cells by prime editing
title: Editing cysteines to figure out what covalent ligands actually do
blurb: ESCAPE uses prime editing to swap the exact cysteines a covalent ligand hits into serines, right in their native genomic context, then reads out how that mutation changes the ligand's cellular phenotype. That gives site-resolved functional calls on covalent ligands at scale, instead of just knowing they bind somewhere on a protein.

original_title: Alternating CO<sub>2</sub> and bicycloalkane copolymerization to circular polyesters
title: A closed-loop plastic from CO2 and bicycloalkanes
blurb: A simple organic catalyst alternates CO2 and bicycloalkanes into high-performance polyesters that can be selectively depolymerized and recycled back to monomers, an actual closed loop rather than the usual 'recyclable in theory' polyester claim.

original_title: Timing-dependent skin toxicity phenotypes during enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab therapy for advanced urothelial carcinoma
title: When the rash shows up during EV/pembrolizumab predicts how it plays out
blurb: A retrospective study of advanced urothelial carcinoma patients on enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, split into no rash, early rash (under a month), and late rash (a month or more). It's the timing of the skin toxicity, not just whether it happens, that gets tracked against treatment outcomes.

original_title: Organopotassium for selective synthesis: Potassium-mediated anti-borylfunctionalization of alkynes
title: Potassium does the anti-selective borylation of alkynes
blurb: An organopotassium-mediated route delivers anti-selective borylfunctionalization of alkynes, a main-group reagent doing a job usually handed to transition-metal catalysts.

original_title: Outside Back Cover: Rhodium(III)‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Synthesis of Silanes and Cyclopropanes From Diazo Compounds Using Chiral α ‐Pinene‐Derived Indenyl Ligands
title: Cover art: rhodium builds chiral silanes and cyclopropanes from diazo compounds
blurb: Cover feature for an asymmetric route from diazo compounds to silanes and cyclopropanes, run with a rhodium(III) catalyst and chiral alpha-pinene-derived indenyl ligands.

original_title: Synergistically enhanced co-adsorption of HMF and hydroxyl on selenium and oxygen dual vacancies in CeO 2 -CuNiSe 2 /NF for high-efficiency HMF electrooxidation
title: HMF electrooxidation gets a vacancy-engineered boost
blurb: CeO2-CuNiSe2/NF with paired oxygen and selenium vacancies grabs HMF and hydroxyl side by side instead of one at a time, and that cooperative adsorption is what pushes the current to 1.23 A/cm2 at 1.5 V vs RHE. A defect-engineering result more than a mechanistic surprise, but that current density is the number that matters.

original_title: How tobacco builds nicotine
title: How tobacco finally welds nicotine's two rings together
blurb: A century-old gap in the pathway closed: nicotinic acid gets glucosylated first, and that turns out to be what activates it for the ring-closing step, with the glucose cut back off once the bond is formed. Two independent studies land on the same mechanism, which is normally a good sign.

original_title: Vicinal‐Diboron Reinforced [9]Helicene Enables Narrowband Blue Circularly Polarized Emitter With Large Dissymmetry Factor and High Device Efficiency
title: A blue circularly polarized emitter that doesn't blur its own narrow edge
blurb: Cranking up a helicene's chirality usually wrecks the narrow emission that makes MR-TADF useful, so B4ONA's move is bolting diboron units on ortho to stiffen the helix without disturbing the electronic structure underneath. Comes with a large dissymmetry factor and, notably, holds up in an actual device, not just in solution.

original_title: Stable Full‐Color and Single‐Phase White Emission in a Family of Isomeric Organic Cu(I) Iodides
title: Five ways to pack the same Cu(I) iodide, five different colors
blurb: Same molecular formula, same monoclinic space group, but the alpha through epsilon polymorphs of (ITPP)2Cu2I4 pack differently enough between them to span full-color emission and land single-phase white light out of one compound family. It also shifts color under heat and chemical stimuli, so the output isn't fixed once you've made it.

original_title: A Validated Method with an Unvalidated Failure Mode: Tetrazolium Endpoints in Reconstructed Human Epidermis Irritation Testing of Nanomaterials
title: The skin-irritation test everyone trusts has a nanomaterial blind spot
blurb: OECD TG 439's tetrazolium endpoint reproduces beautifully lab to lab, 80-100% agreement across validation studies, exactly what you'd want from the test that's been replacing animal irritation testing. But nanomaterials can interfere with the tetrazolium chemistry itself, and the same materials only hit 58% agreement when assessed by ISO 10993-5 cytotoxicity instead. Reproducible isn't the same as correct.

original_title: From nanoscale to clinic: The growing impact of nanotechnology in translational drug delivery
title: A survey lap of nanomedicine, liposomes to nucleic acid delivery
blurb: A review tracing nanotech drug delivery from 1960s liposomes through today's inorganic, polymeric, and lipid platforms, some already commercialized, more still in development. Standard review territory, useful mainly as a map of where the field's actual clinical wins are.

original_title: Design of bifunctional pyridinophane ligands as Mn2+ MRI agents for diagnostic imaging of Alzheimer's disease
title: An MRI stand-in for amyloid PET, if the manganese chelator holds up
blurb: Five bifunctional chelators built on a diaza-pyridinophane scaffold, designed to hold Mn2+ tightly enough to serve as an Alzheimer's MRI contrast agent, a category with zero FDA approvals right now despite PET owning the space. Making a chelator that's stable is a different bar than one that actually reads out amyloid, so this is step one, not the diagnostic itself.

original_title: Photoinduced Copper‐Catalyzed Stereoselective C(sp 3 )‐H Amination Enabled by Preorganized Multiple Noncovalent Interactions
title: Enantioselective C-H amination finally reaches saturated cyclic amines
blurb: Photoinduced copper catalysis aminates the alpha C(sp3)-H of cyclic amines directly, using aromatic and alpha,beta-unsaturated amide nitrogen sources, kept enantioselective by noncovalent interactions preorganizing the transition state. Chiral alpha-amino cyclic amines are a real pharma scaffold, so a direct asymmetric route to them from stable, available nitrogen sources is the actual news here.

original_title: Outside Front Cover: Catalytic C–F Bond Activation at Room Temperature: Enolate Cross‐Couplings Enabled by [Pd(1‐MeNAP)TFA] 2 and LiHMDS
title: C-F bonds finally cross-couple with enolates at room temperature
blurb: This issue's cover: [Pd(1-MeNAP)TFA]2 paired with LiHMDS activates aryl C-F bonds for enolate cross-coupling without any heating. That's the whole pitch going by the cover blurb, but room-temperature C-F activation is usually the hard part of this chemistry.

original_title: Inside Back Cover: High‐Entropy Catalyst Activated Molecular Oxygen for Oxidative Coupling Under Ambient Conditions
title: A high-entropy catalyst wakes up molecular oxygen at room temperature
blurb: Cover feature on a high-entropy catalyst driving oxidative coupling with molecular oxygen itself under ambient conditions, per the cover blurb. Not much more to go on than that, but skipping the usual oxidant workaround is the point.

original_title: Sequential reading of a stepwise-shortened peptide immobilized on nanopore
title: Sequencing peptides by chewing them down one residue at a time
blurb: Nanopore peptide sequencing done by repeatedly clipping one residue off the N-terminus with an enzyme and re-reading the shortened peptide each time, building single-amino-acid resolution out of sequential passes rather than one clean read.

original_title: Intrinsic Phonons as a Dynamic Control Knob for Catalytic Reactivity in 2D Materials
title: Phonons as a knob for tuning catalysis in 2D materials
blurb: A DFT study arguing lattice vibrations aren't just background noise for catalytic activity: exciting specific phonon modes in transition metal dichalcogenides shifts their electronic structure enough to flip direct to indirect bandgaps. In Janus WSSe, driving the A1' mode alone renormalizes the bandgap substantially. All computed so far, nobody's pumped a phonon mode on a real catalyst yet.

original_title: Rapid screening and mechanism analysis of α-amylase inhibitors in apple polyphenols based on immobilized enzyme and HPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS.
title: Screening apple polyphenols for alpha-amylase inhibitors
blurb: An immobilized-enzyme HPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS screen sorts apple polyphenols by how well they inhibit alpha-amylase and digs into the mechanism behind the active ones, the usual blood-sugar-control angle for this class of inhibitor.

original_title: Mapping and Modeling Interfacial pH Dynamics at Enzymatic Microelectrode
title: Enzyme electrodes create their own pH swings right at the surface
blurb: Maps and models how fast redox turnover at an enzyme-modified microelectrode shifts pH right at the interface, even when the bulk solution sits near neutral, and that local swing feeds back onto the enzyme's own activity. Matters for anyone designing biosensors or enzymatic fuel cells who assumed bulk pH was the only pH that counted.

original_title: Study Assessing RLT Using [177Lu]Lu-PentixaTher for Relapsed/Refractory CXCR4+ Acute Leukemia.
title: Lu-177 PentixaTher goes after CXCR4-positive leukemia that already relapsed
blurb: Phase 1/2 at Nantes University Hospital testing the CXCR4-targeted radioligand [177Lu]Lu-PentixaTher in relapsed or refractory acute leukemia that's still CXCR4-positive. Listed active but not recruiting, so it's already running rather than a fresh readout.

original_title: Strategies for the steric shielding of dimetallapolyynes L y M(CC) n ML y : a personal account of approaches to insulated molecular wires and sp carbon allotropes
title: Keeping a 50-carbon wire from falling apart
blurb: A personal retrospective on stabilizing long conjugated polyynes, C48 to C52 and up, by sterically shielding the reactive sp-carbon chain, tracing the arc from the authors' own metal-capped endgroups to the bulky organic caps others adopted later. History of a subfield more than a new result.

original_title: Harnessing Biocatalysis for Green Chemistry: Emerging Innovations and Sustainable Frontiers
title: Where biocatalysis-as-green-chemistry stands right now
blurb: A review of enzyme and microbial catalysis for pharma and fine-chemical synthesis, covering directed evolution, rational design, and machine-learning-assisted enzyme engineering. The pitch is the standard one, shorter routes and cleaner stereochemistry, and it's a round-up of the field rather than a new result.

original_title: Direct Catalytic Propargylic C(sp3)–H Addition to Aldehydes for the Synthesis of Homopropargylic Alcohols
title: Skipping the propargyl reagent prep entirely
blurb: Visible-light LMCT off cheap CrBr3·6H2O activates a propargylic C(sp3)-H bond directly and adds it to aldehydes, making homopropargylic alcohols without prefunctionalizing the alkyne first. Redox-neutral and minimal-input, doing photochemically what usually needs a stoichiometric organometallic reagent.

original_title: Network‐Anchored Nanocages Create Weakly Solvating Electrolytes for Subzero Aqueous Zinc Batteries
title: Stopping zinc batteries from freezing solid
blurb: Fluorinated Zr-based MOP nanocages built into a hydrogel electrolyte grab onto Zn2+ and sterically block water from crowding around it, weakening the ion-solvent interaction that normally freezes aqueous zinc electrolytes and slows the interface at low temperature. Lowers the desolvation barrier without giving up water as the solvent, which is the whole point of going aqueous.

original_title: Curium Reportedly Nears Acquisition Of Lantheus For Approximately $7 Billion - Pulse 2.0
title: Curium reportedly circling Lantheus for about $7 billion
blurb: Reports have Curium closing in on acquiring Lantheus for roughly $7 billion, more consolidation in the radiopharma supply chain if it actually goes through. Still just reported, not confirmed.

original_title: Mechanistic study of novel chemical looping phase separation recovering lithium-ion battery cathode materials with biogas residues
title: Recovering battery cathodes with help from biogas waste
blurb: A chemical looping process that uses leftover biogas digestate to drive phase separation and pull cathode materials back out of spent lithium-ion batteries, tackling two waste streams with one process. Mechanistic study, so it's about how the separation actually works rather than a demonstrated recycling plant.

original_title: Fluorescence Lifetime as a Conformation-Specific Reporter: A Dual-Mode Pt(II) Probe for Parallel G-Quadruplexes in Live Cells
title: A platinum probe that only lights up for parallel G-quadruplexes
blurb: Two cyclometalated Pt(II) complexes, OPtC1 and OPtC2, use fluorescence lifetime rather than plain brightness to call out parallel G-quadruplex DNA, picking it out roughly 27-fold over duplex DNA by end-stacking and groove-binding at once. OPtC1 keeps doing that trick inside live cells, which is the part that actually matters.

original_title: Enzyme‐Mimicking “All‐Nucleotide” G‐Quadruplex Hydrogel as a Dual‐Function Microreactor for Biomimetic Cascade Catalysis
title: A DNA-only hydrogel that acts like an enzyme
blurb: GMP and adenosine phosphate derivatives co-assemble into G-quadruplex networks and hydrogels with built-in catalytic activity, no protein involved. How many phosphates each building block carries, and how acidic it is, sets how the whole thing behaves, turning the gel into a microreactor for cascade reactions made entirely of nucleotides.

original_title: A Structure-Activity Relationship Study of Alpha Synuclein PET Radiotracer M503-1619.
title: Tuning an alpha-synuclein PET tracer
blurb: A structure-activity relationship study on M503-1619, a PET tracer targeting alpha-synuclein, the protein that aggregates in Parkinson's and related synucleinopathies.

original_title: Telix opens Australia's first integrated radiopharmaceutical facility in Melbourne - BiotechDispatch
title: Telix brings radiopharma production onshore in Melbourne
blurb: Telix has opened Australia's first fully integrated radiopharmaceutical facility, in Melbourne, putting production of its own radiopharmaceuticals under one roof domestically.

original_title: Breast Cancer: Diagnosis (PEM) to Assessment of Treatment Response.
title: Positron emission mammography, start to finish
blurb: A review walking through positron emission mammography's role in breast cancer, from initial diagnosis through to reading out whether a treatment is actually working.

original_title: Prostate specific membrane antigen targeted ultrasmall manganese ferrite nanoparticles for PET/MR imaging of prostate cancer.
title: PSMA nanoparticles built to do PET and MRI at once
blurb: Ultrasmall manganese ferrite nanoparticles targeted to PSMA, designed as a combined PET/MR imaging agent for prostate cancer.

original_title: Diffraction-quality, ultraflexible protein single crystals engineered with DNA
title: DNA scaffolding gives protein crystals some bend
blurb: Protein single crystals engineered with DNA that stay diffraction-quality while actually flexing, a combination that normally doesn't come free since rigid crystals are what you need for diffraction in the first place.

original_title: Photocatalysis Towards a Sustainable Future
title: The case for photocatalysis, again
blurb: A review arguing photocatalysis as a route away from fossil-fuel-heavy chemical production. General survey rather than a new result.

original_title: Linker Memory Controls Electrochemical Transformation and Activity of Metal Organic Frameworks
title: MOF electrocatalysts remember their linkers after the linkers are gone
blurb: Ni and NiFe MOFs built from two different linkers, terephthalic acid and 2-methylimidazole, both convert electrochemically into oxyhydroxide catalysts that end up looking chemically similar. But operando tracking shows the original linker still steers which transformation pathway gets taken, and which linker wins out on activity flips depending on conditions, so the framework's starting chemistry survives as a kind of memory even after its structure is gone.

original_title: Solvent Hydrogen Bonding Determines Adsorption Geometry of Trimesic Acid on Cu
title: The solvent decides how trimesic acid sits on copper, not just the metal
blurb: TERS combined with DFT and molecular dynamics settles a running disagreement over trimesic acid's adsorption geometry on Cu, and the deciding factor turns out to be the solvent's hydrogen bonding rather than the metal surface alone. Worth knowing if you use this linker as the standard test case for MOF or catalyst interface chemistry, since orientation control starts upstream of the substrate.

original_title: Inside Front Cover: Metal–Organic Framework‐Gated Biocatalysis Enables Triggered Depolymerization of Melt‐Processed Polyesters
title: A MOF gate that switches plastic-degrading enzymes on
blurb: The idea: cage an enzyme inside a metal-organic framework so it stays dormant until triggered, then it depolymerizes melt-processed polyester on command. It's an Angewandte cover story, so treat it as a proof-of-concept flex on triggered biocatalysis rather than a recycling-plant blueprint just yet.

original_title: This AI ‘Raygun’ can shrink and supersize proteins — opening the door to easy editing
title: An AI raygun that resizes proteins up or down
blurb: A generative model that edits existing proteins by shrinking or supersizing them through a probability-based approach, rather than designing new ones from scratch. Nature's framing it as a step toward easier protein editing generally, but this is a news writeup, so hold off for the actual numbers in the paper.

original_title: Structure‐Guided Redesign of Terminal Deoxynucleotidyl Transferase Enables Scalable Enzymatic DNA Synthesis for Data Storage
title: Fixing the enzyme that's been the bottleneck on DNA data storage
blurb: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase does the actual polymerization in enzymatic DNA synthesis, and it's been held back by low catalytic efficiency and a tendency to aggregate into uselessness. This is a structure-guided redesign aimed at both problems at once, chasing the throughput enzymatic synthesis needs to be a real DNA data storage route instead of just a nice idea on paper.

original_title: Purification of NH₂-PEG₁₂-CH₂COOH after Pd/C azide reduction — TLC system and column advice?
title: Purification of NH₂-PEG₁₂-CH₂COOH after Pd/C azide reduction — TLC system and column advice?
blurb: Hi everyone, I recently synthesized NH₂-PEG₁₂-CH₂COOH by reducing the corresponding azide (N₃-PEG₁₂-CH₂COOH) using Pd/C hydrogenation. After filtering off the catalyst and evaporating the solvent, the product turned out to be quite impure (possibly the starting azide wasn't clean enough). I'm looking for advice on how to purify this compound effectively: Silica gel chromatography — is this a viable option for such a polar, amine-containing PEG derivative? If yes, what solvent system would you recommend? TLC monitoring — what TLC system and visualizing agent work well for amino-PEG-carboxylic a

original_title: The Race for Actinium-225: Inside Oncology’s Fastest-Growing Drug Market - geneonline.com
title: Actinium-225 is now oncology's hottest supply story
blurb: A market rundown on actinium-225 alpha-emitter therapies, pitched as oncology's fastest-growing drug category. Reads like trade press cheerleading; the actual constraint has always been getting enough Ac-225 out of accelerators, not investor appetite.

original_title: Programmable nanomedicine via bioorthogonal molecular engineering
title: Bioorthogonal chemistry turns nanoparticles into programmable devices
blurb: A review on using bioorthogonal handles to bolt functional modules onto nanoparticles after synthesis, trigger payload release on a schedule, and get emergent behavior once particles aggregate or dock onto diseased cells. The pitch is nanomedicines that do more than passively carry cargo. No new data here, just a survey of where the field's landed.

original_title: From stiff and tough to super-soft: Controlling the crosslinking density of 3D printed objects post printing
title: Same resin, dial the crosslink density after printing
blurb: Stereolithography usually forces a tradeoff: dense crosslinking prints fast and sharp but gives brittle parts, sparse crosslinking prints soft but badly. They build in cleavable siloxane crosslinks so density can be cut after the print is done, running the same object from stiff and tough down to super-soft. Useful if the cleavage step doesn't also wreck the regions you wanted to keep stiff.

original_title: Neutral Borate Buffer Activates Diazo for Rapid Protein Labeling
title: Turns out you don't need acid, metal, or light to fire a diazo probe
blurb: Neutral borate buffer alone kicks diazo compounds into their reactive carbene form, labeling proteins in seconds under physiological conditions with no photoactivation or metal catalyst required. It preferentially hits carboxylate side chains, and they've already built an affinity-based covalent probe on top of it. Simpler than the usual diazo activation toolkit, assuming the carboxylate selectivity holds outside their test cases.

original_title: Bis-Tetrazine Fluorogenic (Silicon)-Rhodamine Dyes for Live-Cell Labeling.
title: Bis-tetrazine dyes for live-cell fluorogenic tags
blurb: Silicon-rhodamine dyes carrying two tetrazine handles, built for fluorogenic labeling in live cells so the signal switches on with binding rather than staying always-on.

original_title: Anti-CEACAM5 ADC M9140 in Advanced Solid Tumors (PROCEADE-CRC-01)
title: M9140 keeps rolling in colorectal cancer, still just phase 1
blurb: PROCEADE-CRC-01 is the phase 1 trial of M9140, EMD Serono's anti-CEACAM5 antibody-drug conjugate, in advanced solid tumors; the colorectal cancer arm is active but no longer recruiting. Not much news here beyond the status update itself.

original_title: Chelatron: Charting Chemical Space with Agentic AI for Metal-Ligand Discovery
title: An agentic AI that goes looking for its own metal-ligand data
blurb: Chelatron uses LLM-driven agentic workflows to decide what new experiments to run for metal-ligand discovery, aimed at the low-data regime where standard data-driven models stall out from sparse, fragmentary priors. The pitch is a system that picks its own next data point instead of just fitting whatever's already measured. Whether that beats a chemist's intuition on where to sample next isn't shown here.

original_title: Surface-Confinement Effect Enables Bioorthogonal Drug Release in Tumors.
title: Surface confinement as the on-switch for bioorthogonal drug release
blurb: The trigger for releasing drug in tumors here is confining the bioorthogonal reaction to a surface instead of letting it run free in solution. That's the whole hook: geometry doing the selectivity work rather than a new chemical handle.

original_title: A Phase 2, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Safety and Efficacy of Dose-Intensified Versus Standard Dosing Regimens of [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA-597 in mCRPC (OPTIMAL-PSMA).
title: Does more Lu-177-PSMA actually beat the standard dose in mCRPC?
blurb: OPTIMAL-PSMA is a phase 2 randomized trial pitting dose-intensified against standard dosing of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-597 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, open-label, checking both safety and efficacy. A straightforward more-vs-standard dosing question rather than a new ligand or mechanism.

original_title: Synthesis of nanoporous titanium aerogel through sol-gel method for efficient purification of helium-3
title: A titanium aerogel built to scrub tritium out of helium-3
blurb: Sol-gel titanium aerogel, made via supercritical ethanol drying, tuned across titanium content plus adsorption temperature and pressure, to pull trace tritium out of helium-3 streams. It's basically an optimization study on adsorption conditions, with the eventual use case being cleaner He-3 for fusion fuel.

original_title: Application of Theranostics in Thyroid Cancer Management.
title: A status check on theranostics in thyroid cancer
blurb: A review of where diagnostic imaging paired with matched radionuclide treatment currently stands in thyroid cancer care. No new data, just a survey of the field.

original_title: Reshaping Chiral Self-Assemblies Through Alkyne-Involved Click Chemistry.
title: Click chemistry as a knob for chiral self-assembly
blurb: Alkyne-based click reactions used to reorganize chiral self-assembled structures after the fact rather than just building them from scratch. Light on specifics beyond that framing.

original_title: Performance Evaluation of Single- and Double-Layer CZT Compton Cameras for (225)Ac Imaging.
title: Single-layer vs double-layer CZT cameras for imaging Actinium-225
blurb: An instrumentation shootout, not a clinical one: single- versus double-layer CZT Compton cameras benchmarked for imaging Ac-225, the alpha-emitter everyone's short on good dosimetry tools for.

original_title: A Phase 2, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Safety and Efficacy of Dose-Intensified Versus Standard Dosing Regimens of [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-597 in mCRPC (OPTIMAL-PSMA)
title: Pushing the Lu-177-PSMA-597 dose higher in mCRPC, and seeing what breaks
blurb: OPTIMAL-PSMA, a phase 2 open-label randomized trial, tests dose-intensified against standard dosing of Lu-177-PSMA-597 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, safety and efficacy both on the table.

original_title: Tumor and Organ Dose Estimates from 177 Lu-PSMA-617 Therapy in Patients with Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Results from the RESIST-PC Phase 2 Trial
title: What Lu-177-PSMA-617 actually delivers to tumors and organs
blurb: Dosimetry numbers out of the RESIST-PC phase 2 trial: tumor and organ dose estimates for Lu-177-PSMA-617 therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients.

original_title: A Comprehensive Review on RP-HPLC Method Development and Validation for Simultaneous Estimation of Linagliptin and Empagliflozin in Bulk Drug and Pharmaceutical Dosage Forms
title: A review of RP-HPLC methods for the linagliptin-empagliflozin combo pill
blurb: Linagliptin and empagliflozin get dosed together as a fixed-dose combo for type 2 diabetes, so this rounds up the RP-HPLC methods used to measure both at once for QC and stability testing. Not new chemistry, just a survey of the assay landscape.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Chemical Rescue Serves as a Predictive Proxy for Glycosynthase Activity on Glycosidic Bonds via a Shared Glycosyl Oxocarbenium Transition State
title: Skip the azido-sugar screen, use chemical rescue instead
blurb: Screening glycosynthase mutants normally means feeding them expensive activated azido-sugar donors, which throttles directed evolution. Here chemical rescue, azide restoring hydrolytic activity in nucleophile-dead mutants, stands in as a proxy for the real glycosynthase activity, run through an azide-responsive E. coli biosensor on a site-saturation library of Thermotoga maritima fucosidase. A cheap trick to unclog the bottleneck, if the correlation holds beyond this one enzyme.

original_title: [(18)F]PSMA-1007 PET-Based Recurrence Site Distribution and Predictors of Metastatic Disease in Patients With Biochemical Recurrence of Prostate Cancer.
title: Where prostate cancer comes back, mapped by PSMA-1007 PET
blurb: PSMA-1007 PET scans used to chart where recurrence shows up in biochemically relapsed prostate cancer patients, and what predicts metastatic rather than local disease.

original_title: Photoinduced Copper‐Catalyzed Stereoselective C(sp 3 )‐H Amination Enabled by Preorganized Multiple Noncovalent Interactions
title: Finally doing asymmetric C–H amination on saturated cyclic amines
blurb: Chiral alpha-amino cyclic amines are the kind of scaffold that shows up everywhere in bioactive molecules, but nobody had managed asymmetric C(sp3)-H amination on them directly. This gets there with a photoinduced copper catalyst and preorganized noncovalent interactions steering the enantioselectivity, using aromatic and unsaturated amides as the nitrogen source instead of exotic reagents.

original_title: Merging Criegee intermediate with C(sp3)−C(sp3) cross coupling
title: Splicing Criegee intermediates into C(sp3)-C(sp3) cross coupling
blurb: Criegee intermediates are the peroxo species everyone's spotted since the earliest ozonolysis and Baeyer-Villiger work, but here they get pulled into a new C(sp3)-C(sp3) cross coupling via an anti-Giese addition. The mechanistic case is solid: 18O2 labeling shows the tetrahedral peroxo intermediate spitting out 16O=C=O18, nailing down the pathway rather than just proposing it.

original_title: Light and Acid‐Base Dual‐Regulated Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization With ppb Concentrations of Zwitterionic Photocatalysts
title: A photocatalyst you can switch with light or pH, at parts-per-billion loadings
blurb: Zwitterionic benzimidazolate/naphthoimidazolate photocatalysts for ATRP, where an electron-withdrawing methylpyridinium group lets the reducing anion form under just mild base or neutral conditions. Two independent handles, light and acid/base, on the same polymerization, and the reported quenching rate constants are fast enough to run at ppb catalyst loadings.

original_title: Assessing the physiological S nitrosoproteome reveals nitric oxide mediated regulatory networks in rice
title: Where nitric oxide leaves its signature across the rice proteome
blurb: A survey mapping the physiological S-nitrosoproteome in rice, tying reversible S-nitrosylation to regulatory networks behind seed dormancy, stress responses, and development. Mostly a mapping exercise, connecting NO signaling to specific protein targets rather than new mechanism.

original_title: Engineering Receptor-Mediated Cell-Surface Mobility with Phage-Inspired DNA Tetrapods
title: DNA tetrapods built to wander across a bacterial surface, not just stick to it
blurb: Phages don't bind their receptor and stay put, they use weak reversible contacts to crawl across a bacterial surface hunting a better spot before committing. This engineers DNA tetrapods to copy that receptor-mediated mobility, deliberately going for weak multivalent binding instead of the usual tight multivalent display.

original_title: Modular Cyano-fluoroalkylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by Photoinduced Fe-LMCT Catalysis
title: Turning trifluoroacetic acid into a radical fluoroalkyl source with iron and light
blurb: An iron-photocatalyzed cyano-fluoroalkylation of unactivated alkenes that pulls the fluoroalkyl radical straight from cheap carboxylic acids, trifluoroacetic acid included, via LMCT off an Fe(III)-carboxylate complex, then caps the other end with tosyl cyanide. Cheap iron and cheap acid standing in for the usual expensive fluoroalkyl reagents.

original_title: The Jekyll and Hyde Nature of Tetrazoles in Polymer Science: From Intrinsic Electronic Duality to Programmable Macromolecular Function
title: Tetrazoles as chemistry's two-faced building block, stable until you flip the switch
blurb: A perspective on tetrazoles' polarized electronic structure: aromatic and persistent most of the time, but latently reactive once triggered, with the substitution pattern setting which face shows up. More a framing piece than new data, aimed at using that duality for programmable polymer behavior.

original_title: Tumor and Organ Dose Estimates from (177)Lu-PSMA-617 Therapy in Patients with Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer: Results from the RESIST-PC Phase 2 Trial.
title: Actual dosimetry numbers for Lu-177-PSMA-617, not just response rates
blurb: Tumor and organ dose estimates from Lu-177-PSMA-617 therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, out of the RESIST-PC Phase 2 trial. The kind of absorbed-dose accounting that usually gets left out in favor of PSA numbers.

original_title: Sulfone Activation Triggered by Iodide Anion for Photoinduced Fluoroalkylations
title: Iodide anion filling in for the photocatalyst
blurb: A catalyst-free route to radical fluoroalkylation via an electron donor-acceptor complex: cheap iodide as the electron donor, fluoroalkyl sulfones as the radical source, no metal photocatalyst or dye needed. The appeal here is what's missing from the reaction, not what's in it.

original_title: Glyoxal induces DNA-Protein Crosslinking in Cells
title: Glyoxal, made by your own metabolism, staples proteins straight onto DNA
blurb: Glyoxal already modifies DNA and proteins separately into AGEs linked to diabetes, cancer, and aging, but whether it also forms DNA-protein crosslinks, a nastier kind of damage, was unresolved. This shows it does, in cells, and glyoxal is made endogenously during normal metabolism, so no exotic exposure is required.

original_title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From A Main Group Centre
title: Getting a p-block element to pull off a transition metal's signature move
blurb: Reductive elimination is routine for transition metals and stubbornly hard for main group elements, usually forced only through careful ligand and geometry design. This gets a main group center to do it photocatalytically instead, light substituting for the usual ligand-tuning gymnastics.

original_title: Protein-confined imidazolium intermediates enable diverse biocatalytic C–C and C–N bond formations
title: Enzymes that cage an imidazolium intermediate to steer which bond it forms
blurb: Small nucleophilic catalysts can run allylic transfer chemistry, but regio- and stereocontrol is usually hard to pin down. This engineers a family of allylic transferase enzymes that confine the key imidazolium intermediate inside the protein, using that confinement to direct both C-C and C-N bond formation.

original_title: Carbonyl stress by glyceraldehyde promotes glycation of nuclear non-muscle myosins in DNA-protein crosslink assemblies.
title: Sugar stress glycates myosin right where DNA gets crosslinked
blurb: Glyceraldehyde-driven carbonyl stress glycates nuclear non-muscle myosins found in DNA-protein crosslink assemblies, tying reactive carbonyl damage to another nuclear structural protein caught up in crosslink formation. No mechanism or downstream consequence given beyond that.

original_title: Coordination‐Tuned Iridium Single‐Atom Nanozymes Boost Multienzyme Activity for Colorimetric Sensing
title: A pinch of sulfur turns an iridium catalyst into a multi-enzyme mimic
blurb: Bolting a sulfur atom onto the usual Ir-N-C single-atom scaffold gives an asymmetric Ir-N3S1 site that DFT says retunes the electronics at the iridium center, and that alone boosts several enzyme-mimetic activities in the same particle. Aimed at colorimetric sensing, one catalyst doing the work of a few reagents.

original_title: Revisiting Coulombic Efficiency Paradigm: Electrolyte Additive Design for Lithium Metal Batteries
title: Coulombic efficiency numbers on lithium metal don't just track additive structure
blurb: A dig into why Li°||Cu° coulombic efficiency doesn't line up cleanly with fluorinated additive structure, pairing cycling statistics with composition and atomistic characterization to figure out what's actually driving CE. Useful if you've been picking additives on structure alone and getting inconsistent results.

original_title: Difunctionalization of Alkenes via Photoinduced Oxidative Radical‐Polar Crossover
title: A review of what radical-polar crossover has done for alkene difunctionalization
blurb: A survey of alkene difunctionalization built on photoinduced oxidative radical-polar crossover, pairing radical initiation with a polar finish to build 1,2-difunctionalized products under mild light-driven conditions. Sorts the growing pile of ORPC methods into categories rather than reporting new chemistry.

original_title: Pairing a Zn 1 O 1 Monomer With Oxide Supports via Dual Interfacial Metal–Oxygen Bonding for Stable Conversion of Syngas to Light Olefins
title: Zn1O1 on oxide supports needs two bonds, not one, to survive
blurb: Isolated Zn1O1 monomers on oxide supports only stay put when both interfacial bonds, Zn-O' and O-M', form properly. Supports with too weak an oxygen vacancy formation energy can't anchor the oxide monomer, so it falls apart during syngas-to-light-olefins runs. A stability recipe specific to oxide monomers, distinct from single metal atoms on the same supports.

original_title: In Silico to In Cerebro—Development of the Orexin Receptor Antagonist “Photorexant” for Photomodulation In Vitro and in Mouse Brains
title: Photorexant lets you switch orexin signaling on and off with light
blurb: A photoswitchable azobenzene version of suvorexant, the FDA-approved dual orexin antagonist, built by structure-based design plus a new computational fragmentation workflow, blocking OX1R and OX2R in one light state and not the other. Tested in vitro and in mouse brains as a tool for dissecting orexin signaling, not as a drug candidate.

original_title: Evidence of Eley–Rideal mechanism in Cu-catalysed CO<sub>2</sub> electroreduction in flow cells with a protective layer
title: Cu CO2 reduction in flow cells looks like an Eley-Rideal reaction after all
blurb: A porous protective layer isolates the copper-catalyzed C-C coupling step in flow cells, and the resulting data point to an Eley-Rideal mechanism, one adsorbed species reacting with one from solution, rather than two adsorbed intermediates meeting on the surface. Cell architecture and mass transport turn out to matter more than prior setups could pin down.

original_title: Nickel nanoparticles encapsulated inside mesoporous MoO<sub>2</sub> for industrially stable anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis
title: Ni nanoparticles boxed inside MoO2 give AEM electrolysis a stable HER catalyst
blurb: NiMo catalysts are already good at hydrogen evolution in alkaline electrolyte, they just don't last. Encapsulating Ni nanoparticles inside mesoporous MoO2 gives a Ni/MoO2 cathode that holds up at industrially relevant stability for anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis.

original_title: Flipped Spin‐State Resists Cobalt Poisoning for the Durable Electrocatalytic Deuteration of N ‐Heterocyclic Compounds
title: Flipping cobalt's spin state keeps it from getting poisoned during deuteration
blurb: Electrocatalytic deuteration of N-heterocycles usually kills its own catalyst, since the metal binds too hard to the nitrogen lone pair and deactivates. A Mn3Co7 alloy forces cobalt from high-spin to low-spin, pushing electrons into antibonding orbitals that weaken that binding, so the catalyst keeps working. Deuterated N-heterocycles are drug-development scaffolds, so durability here is the whole point.

original_title: Recent advances in the asymmetric catalytic construction of chiral indenols
title: A review of how chemists build chiral indenols catalytically
blurb: A rundown of transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric annulation routes to chiral indenols, tracing early methods through current strategies, intermediates, and frameworks. Indenols turn up constantly in drugs and natural products, so this is a map of how people get the stereocenter, not a new reaction.

original_title: Combined 177Lu-FAP-2286 Therapy and Immunotherapy in Metastatic Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
title: 177Lu-FAP-2286 plus immunotherapy, tried in esophageal cancer
blurb: A FAP-targeted radioligand paired with immunotherapy, used against metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Reads like a case report rather than a trial, so it's one data point, not a strategy yet.

original_title: A Rigid Molecular Triangle as an Ultrafast and Highly Selective Transmembrane Li + Channel
title: A rigid molecular triangle that moves Li+ faster than gramicidin moves K+
blurb: A C3-symmetric pyromellitic diimide triangle forms a single-molecule Li+ channel, 2.2 nm tall with a 4.1 Å pore lined in carbonyl oxygens. Single-channel conductance hits 57.4 pS, 2.5x what gramicidin A does for K+, with a selectivity ratio around 50 against other ions. Getting both speed and selectivity out of one design is the rare part.

original_title: Light-Written, Self-Erasing Hydrogels for On-the-Fly Reconfigurable Microfluidics
title: Hydrogels you draw with light and that erase themselves
blurb: Blue light hits a water-soluble spiropyran photoacid, drops the local pH, and that's enough to trigger the dipeptide Fmoc-Leu-Gly to self-assemble into a fibrous hydrogel wherever it's shone. Cut the light and it erases itself, so a microfluidic channel layout can be redrawn on the fly instead of building a new chip each time.

original_title: Low‐Energy Photons in Radical Chemistry: From Deep‐Red to Near‐Infrared Radical Generation for Organic Synthesis
title: Doing radical chemistry with photons too weak to normally bother
blurb: A look at generating radicals for synthesis using deep-red and near-infrared light instead of the usual higher-energy visible or UV, via chromophores and catalysts built to actually absorb that weak end of the spectrum.

original_title: Solvent and Ligand Control of Long‐Lived Charge‐Separated States in Cerium(IV) Photocatalysis
title: What actually keeps a cerium photooxidant's charges apart
blurb: Broadband transient absorption on cerium(IV) ammonium nitrate, femtoseconds to microseconds, shows that in acetonitrile an LMCT event produces a charge-separated state, free NO3• radicals plus Ce(III), that survives 40 µs. Switch to a protic solvent like methanol and that productive channel gets shut down. Solvent choice isn't a minor detail here, it's the whole mechanism.
